result.title: AutoFraming: Synthesizing Dynamic Frames of C Code with LLMs
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown considerable promise in synthesizing formal specifications from source code. However, existing approaches primarily focus on functional contracts and loop invariants, while largely neglecting frame conditions, which specify the memory locations that may or may not be modified during execution and constitute an essential part of formal specifications. To address this limitation, we propose an LLM-based approach for synthesizing ACSL frame specifications alongside functional contracts from C code. Our approach analyzes code property graphs (CPGs) to extract frame-relevant information from the input code and leverages this information to guide the LLM in generating accurate frame conditions. The resulting specifications capture both region-separation constraints and data dependencies that govern variable modifications. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. On a benchmark of 84 ACSL-compliant functions from non-trivial real-world systems, our method successfully synthesizes error-free frame specifications for 92.9% of the functions, representing a 179% relative improvement over state-of-the-art techniques. On a second benchmark consisting of 51 functions, the success rate increases from 80.4% to 96.1%. Furthermore, when integrated as an auxiliary component into existing LLM-based ACSL-synthesis frameworks, our approach improves frame-specification generation performance by up to 61.9%.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 AutoFraming，利用代码属性图（CPG）提取与帧条件相关的信息来引导 LLM 从 C 代码合成 ACSL 帧规格，并在真实系统函数基准上评估其成功率与对现有框架的增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉/多模态推理无直接关联，但其用静态分析显式刻画「哪些状态允许被修改」的分离与依赖约束来条件化生成，可能为 LVR 中状态更新、侧效应与监督表示的显式建模提供可供核查的线索。
